concept_gloss.applicability: Nesnenin insanı andıran görünüşünü, ekili alandaki yerini ve hayvanları ürkütme işlevini doğal biçimde karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: İnsan biçimini, tarla bağlamını ve hayvanları ürkütüp uzak tutma işlevini korur.

concept_map.definition: Ekili alanın ortasına insan görünümünde dikilen, yaban hayvanlarını ve kuşları ürküterek üründen uzak tutmaya yarayan nesnedir.

facets.statement: Nesne ekili alanın içine dikilir ve insanı andıran bir görünüşe sahiptir.
İşlevi yaban hayvanlarını ve kuşları ürkütüp ekinden uzak tutmaktır.

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal kovulmuş bir insanı ya da kurdu değil, ekili alana dikilen insan biçimli koruyucu nesneyi anlatır.
identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak sözü ekinlerin arasına insan görünümünde dikilen ve yaban hayvanları ile kuşları ürküten bir nesneyi açıkça tanımlar. Verilen tarla korkuluğu çerçevesi bu nesne, yer ve işlev birliğini doğru biçimde korur.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalnız kaynakta verilen insan biçimli tarla nesnesini kapsar ve aynı ses biçimine sahip dışlanmış kişi anlamını bu dala taşımaz.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; insan biçimli yapay nesne ve tarım aracı karşılaştırmaları yararlı bulundu, diğer adaylar nesnenin görünüşü ile koruma işlevini paylaşmadı.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalın nesnesi tarımsal koruma için hayvanları ürkütür; komşu dalın nesnesini ise tapınma amacı kurar, bu yüzden sıradan kullanımda birbirlerinin yerine geçmezler.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak nesne ekili alana dikilir ve hayvanları ürküterek ürünü korumaya yarar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu nesne ağaçtan veya metalden yapılabilen ve kendisine tapılan bir gövdedir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da insanı andırabilen, dik duran ve insanlarca yapılmış bir nesneyi anlatabilir.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Ortaklık yalnız tarım alanıdır; odak nesne görünüşüyle hayvanları uzak tutarken komşu araç ürünün elle savrulup temizlenmesinde kullanılır.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak nesne tarlada sabit durup kuşları ve yaban hayvanlarını ürkütür.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu nesne, harmandaki ürünü savurup taneyi samandan ayırmaya yarayan parmaklı bir araçtır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki nesne de ekin üretimi ve ürünün korunup işlenmesi alanında kullanılır.

branches.source_phrase_ar: اللعين ما يتخذ في المزارع كهيئة رجل (ayn;tahdhib); الرجل اللعين شيء ينصب وسط المزارع تستطرد به الوحوش (sihah); كهيئة خيال يذعر منه السباع والطيور (tahdhib)

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak tanımı, ekili alana insan biçiminde dikilen ve yaban hayvanlarıyla kuşları ürkütüp uzaklaştıran nesnedir.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه اللعين بمعنى الشيء المنصوب في المزارع كهيئة رجل ليذعر السباع والطيور أو يطرد الوحوش
branches.what_is_not_ar: ليس الرجل الملعون ولا الذئب الطريد ولا اللعن بالدعاء

concept_gloss.applicability: Yer türünü, ortak kullanımı ve o yeri dışkılayarak kirleten kişiye yönelen tepkiyi birlikte açıklar.

error_profile.preserves: Ortak kullanım yerini, dışkılama koşulunu ve kirletene yönelen kötülük dileğini korur.

concept_gloss.text: dışkılayan kişiye kötülük dilenen ortak kullanım yeri

concept_map.definition: Yol kenarı, insanların konakladığı yer veya ağaç gölgesi gibi ortak kullanılan ve birinin dışkılaması yüzünden başkalarının o kişiye kötülük dilediği yerdir.

facets.statement: Gönderim, insanların geçtiği, konakladığı veya gölgelendiği ortak kullanım yerlerinedir.
Yol kenarı, konaklama yeri ve ağaç gölgesi bu yer türünün verilen örnekleridir.
Adlandırma, bu yerlerde dışkılayan kişinin başkalarını rahatsız etmesi ve onların kötülük dileğine uğramasıyla açıklanır.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Yol ve gölgelik örneklerini tek tek saymadan yerin toplumsal işlevini açıklayan bağlamlarda kullanılabilir.

error_profile.adds: Tepkiyi yalnız kötülük dilemekle sınırlamayıp her türlü öfkeye genişletir.
error_profile.preserves: Ortak yerin kirletilmesinin başkalarında ağır tepki doğurmasını korur.

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal karşılıklı bir söz eylemini değil, kirletilmesi insanları rahatsız edip kirletene kötülük dilettiren ortak kullanım yerlerini anlatır.
identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak sözü yol kenarlarını, insanların konakladığı yerleri ve ağaç gölgelerini sayar; bu yerlerde dışkılayan kişiye insanların kötülük dilediğini de adlandırmanın gerekçesi olarak verir. Dal çerçevesi yer ile tepki arasındaki bağı doğru biçimde kurar.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: dışkılama yüzünden kirletene kötülük dilenen yol ve gölgelik yerler
kirleten kişiye kötülük dilenen yol kenarı veya konak yeri

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım kaynakta sayılan ortak kullanım yerlerini ve dışkılama nedeniyle doğan tepkiyi birlikte korur; karşılıklı söz eylemi anlamını içeri almaz.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Adayların tamamı incelendi; hiçbiri ortak bir yerin dışkılamayla kirletilmesi ve kirletene kötülük dilenmesi çekirdeğini paylaşmadığından yayımlanacak yararlı bir karşılaştırma bulunmadı.
branches.source_phrase_ar: المَلاعِن قارعة الطريق ومنزل الناس (sihah); المَلاعِن جواد الطريق وظلال الشجر ينزلها الناس؛ يلعنون من جلس للغائط عليها (tahdhib)

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak tanımı yol, konaklama yeri ve gölgelik gibi ortak alanları kapsar; buralarda dışkılayan kişiye yönelen kötülük dileği adlandırmanın gerekçesidir.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه المَلاعِن بمعنى جواد الطريق وظلال الشجر ومنازل الناس التي يتأذى بها الناس من الحدث فيلعنون فاعله
branches.what_is_not_ar: ليست الملاعنة بين الأشخاص ولا صيغة اللعان بين الزوجين

concept_gloss.applicability: Verilen seslenişin muhatabı kötü davranıştan uzak tutan içeriğini ve saygılı hitap değerini birlikte karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: Muhatabın kınanacak ve kötülük dilenecek bir davranıştan uzak olduğu bildirimini korur.

concept_gloss.text: Kınanıp kötülük dilenecek bir iş yapmazsın

concept_map.definition: Muhatabın kınanıp kendisine kötülük dilenecek bir iş yapmadığını bildiren saygılı bir sesleniştir. Özellikle hükümdarı selamlarken onun böyle bir davranıştan uzak olduğu söylenir.

facets.statement: Söz, muhatabın kınanmayı ve kendisine kötülük dilenmesini gerektiren bir iş yapmadığını bildirir.
Bu bildirim hükümdara yöneltilen saygılı bir selamlama ve seslenme biçimi olarak kullanılabilir.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Saygılı seslenişin kötülük dileme arka planını bağlam zaten gösterdiğinde kısa bir karşılık olabilir.

error_profile.loses: Davranışın muhataba kötülük dilenmesine yol açacağı yönünü açıkça söylemez.
error_profile.preserves: Muhatabın kınanacak davranıştan uzak olduğu bildirimini korur.

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal muhataba kötülük dilemez; onun kınanmayı ve kötülük dilenmesini gerektirecek bir iş yapmadığını bildiren bir sesleniştir.
identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak sözü, muhatabın kınanıp kendisine kötülük dilenecek bir iş yapmadığını bildiren ve hükümdarlara seslenirken kullanılan bir deyişi açıklar. Dal çerçevesi sözün kötülük dilemediğini, tersine buna yol açacak davranışı muhataptan uzak tuttuğunu doğru biçimde belirtir.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: Kınanıp kötülük dilenecek bir iş yapmazsın

lexicalization_scope.note: Anlam yalnız verilen kalıplaşmış seslenişe bağlıdır; kökün yalın biçimine genel bir aklanma veya övgü anlamı yüklenmez.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; yalnız aynı kökün sözlü kötülük dileme dalı, bu seslenişin olumsuzlama işlevini açıklayan yararlı bir karşıtlık sağladı.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal muhataba kötülük yöneltmez ve onun böyle bir sözü hak edecek iş yapmadığını söyler; komşu dal ise kötülük dileğinin veya sövgünün kendisidir.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal muhatabın kötülük dilenmeyi gerektirecek davranıştan uzak olduğunu bildiren saygılı bir sesleniştir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal başka birine gerçekten kötülük dilemeyi veya ağır biçimde sövmeyi anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal aynı kötülük dileme senaryosuna katılır, fakat farklı söz eylemleri gerçekleştirir.

branches.source_phrase_ar: أبيت اللعن أي لا تأتي أمرا تلحى عليه وتلعن (ayn); تحيي ملوكها بأن تقول للملك أبيت اللعن؛ أبيت أيها الملك أن تأتي أمرا تلعن عليه (tahdhib)

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak açıklaması, sözün muhatabı kınanacak ve kendisine kötülük dilenecek davranıştan uzak tuttuğunu; hükümdarlara seslenirken selamlama işlevi taşıdığını bildirir.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه قولهم أبيت اللعن تحية أو خطابا بمعنى نفي أن يأتي المخاطب أمرا يلام عليه ويلعن
branches.what_is_not_ar: ليس دعاء باللعن على المخاطب ولا وقوع اللعن عليه

text.arabic_uthmani: وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لَكَ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ أَحَاطَ بِٱلنَّاسِ ۚ وَمَا جَعَلْنَا ٱلرُّءْيَا ٱلَّتِىٓ أَرَيْنَٰكَ إِلَّا فِتْنَةًۭ لِّلنَّاسِ وَٱلشَّجَرَةَ ٱلْمَلْعُونَةَ فِى ٱلْقُرْءَانِ ۚ وَنُخَوِّفُهُمْ فَمَا يَزِيدُهُمْ إِلَّا طُغْيَٰنًۭا كَبِيرًۭا

baseline.text: Bir zaman sana, Rabbin insanları kuşatmıştır, demiştik. Sana gösterdiğimiz görüntüyü ve Kur'an'da lanetlenen ağacı insanlar için yalnızca bir sınama yaptık. Onları korkutuyoruz, fakat bu onların büyük azgınlığından başka bir şeyi artırmıyor.

findings.text: Görüntü ve lanetli ağaç, Allah'ın kuşatıcı bilgisi içinde tepkiyi açığa çıkaran sınama araçlarıdır; uyarının azgınlığı artırması bu alanın dışına kaçışı değil, gizli yönelişin taşarak görünür olmasını anlatır.

activation_trace.role: Complete enclosure in knowledge and possession supplies the controlled scope of the assay.
Showing and making visible supplies the exposed specimen within that scope.
Testing metal or a person turns the displayed material into a diagnostic assay.
Putting fear into another supplies the applied pressure intended to induce caution.
Increase and growth marks the counter-effect produced in the recipients.
Water rising into a sweeping force materializes transgression as an amplifying overflow.

changed_reading.after: The ayah stages a contained diagnostic feedback loop in which signs and warning expose the recipients' disposition by eliciting an enlarging overflow.
changed_reading.before: The ayah juxtaposes divine enclosure, two troubling signs, warning, and greater disobedience.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: أَحَاطَ ... الرُّءْيَا ... فِتْنَةً ... نُخَوِّفُهُمْ ... يَزِيدُهُمْ ... طُغْيَانًا
baseline_models.mechanism: The Lord's complete enclosure contains a staged exposure: showing supplies the specimen, fitna assays it, warning applies pressure, and the audience response both reveals and enlarges boundary-crossing overflow.

activation_trace.role: Spoken utterance initiates the transmission chain addressed to the messenger.
Making something assume a state frames the vision as assigned test material rather than an accidental image.
Dream vision supplies one medium while the paired causative showing makes its transmission explicit.
Gathering and joining makes the Qur'anic tree part of a collected communicative medium.
Human society, repeated on both sides of the sign clause, supplies the public reception field.
The stemmed tree supplies the second concrete sign carried in recitation.
Expulsion under displeasure gives that second sign its warning charge.

changed_reading.after: The ayah coordinates visual showing and recited object as two stages of one public sign-transmission problem.
changed_reading.before: A private vision and a cursed tree are two unrelated objects that happen to test people.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: قُلْنَا لَكَ ... الرُّءْيَا الَّتِي أَرَيْنَاكَ ... لِلنَّاسِ ... فِي الْقُرْآنِ
baseline_models.mechanism: Utterance, making, vision, showing, and gathered recitation form a transmission chain. A display given to one addressee becomes a public test through two media, the vision and the tree as recited sign, while the repeated people marks its social reception field.

activation_trace.role: Nourishment and growth, from the packet's split mapped root, supplies the constructive growth pole.
The stemmed tree gives the opposed growths an ecological body.
Increase and growth transfers the growth image to the recipients' reaction.
Water exceeding its measure turns the reaction's growth into material overflow.
Magnitude marks the countergrowth as no longer contained within a small deviation.

changed_reading.after: The closing clause can be pictured as countergrowth: warning meets a cultivated human field but the resistant growth swells into a flood.
changed_reading.before: The closing clause reports an abstract increase in rebellion.

baseline_models.mechanism: A form-distant growth branch under the split mapping of rabb resonates with tree, increase, and flood-like transgression. The focus can therefore carry two opposed growths: encompassing nurture and an audience response that swells beyond its boundary.

activation_trace.role: Turning something through different states supplies repeated communicative variation.
Reading and recitation locates that variation in the same medium named in the focus.
A reminder that causes recollection supplies the intended reception effect.
Increase and growth supplies the exact counter-effect operator repeated in the focus.
Drawing away from a thing names the earlier resistant output of that operator.
Crossing the limit intensifies the earlier aversion into active boundary violation.

changed_reading.after: The focus is the sharper recurrence of an established pattern in which communicative variation is converted by resistant reception into withdrawal and then overflowing transgression.
changed_reading.before: The warning in 17:60 unexpectedly causes a one-time worsening.

context_deltas.mechanism: Verse 17:41 is a compact rehearsal of the focus: Qur'anic material is varied for recollection, yet it only increases aversion. The focus replaces varied reminder with vision, tree, and warning, and replaces aversion with great overflow, making the paradox a repeated reception pattern rather than an isolated failure.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies matched grammar, medium, and counter-effect; I infer a recurrent receiver-side transformation law, while the live alternative is two independent descriptions that merely share diction.
structural_cues: Both 17:41 and 17:60 use ما ... إلا around يزيدهم ... إلا, with Qur'anic communication before the increase and a resistant state after it.

activation_trace.role: Seeking a thing supplies directed movement toward a superior center.
The elevated royal throne supplies the vertical center toward which the hypothetical rivals move.
An extended traversable path turns hierarchy into a spatial route.
Height expressed as greatness and domination marks the vertical quality denied to human claims.
Magnitude forms the exact adjectival echo later attached to transgression.
Crossing the limit turns the recipients' rise into illegitimate vertical excess.
Greatness and self-exaltation qualifies that excess as counterfeit grandeur.

changed_reading.after: Great transgression becomes an attempted upward overreach inside the very enclosure that makes rival height impossible.
changed_reading.before: Great transgression means severe disobedience without a spatial mechanism.

context_deltas.mechanism: Claimed rival gods would seek a route toward the possessor of the elevated throne, while God is exalted with great elevation above what people say. The focus's great transgression then reads spatially as a counterfeit rise that crosses its proper limit.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the shared adjective and a vertical throne-path sequence; I infer that the echo spatializes transgression as counterfeit elevation, while the live alternative is that كبيرًا only intensifies two unrelated nouns.
structural_cues: Verse 17:43 closes with عُلُوًّا كَبِيرًا and the focus closes with طُغْيَانًا كَبِيرًا after the same human speech controversy.

activation_trace.role: Reading and recitation supplies the communicative event at which the barrier appears.
A covering barrier supplies blocked access despite an audible recitation.
Covering makes the barrier itself unavailable to ordinary inspection.
Protective concealment locates the occlusion at the heart's reception surface.
Weight in the ear adds an auditory obstruction to the hidden barrier.
Turning away converts internal occlusion into outward refusal.
Aversion as drawing away supplies the observable reception result.
Showing anchors the revised model in the focus's visual disclosure.
Assay makes the disclosure diagnostic of the occluded receiver rather than merely informative.

changed_reading.after: The signs test a layered reception apparatus in which disclosure and concealment coexist, so increased transgression is the output of an occluded interface.
changed_reading.before: The signs are clear inputs that people consciously reject.

context_deltas.mechanism: Recitation is followed by an unseen covered barrier, protected coverings over hearts, weight in ears, and turning backs in aversion. The focus's shown vision is therefore not simply evidence made available; visual and recited disclosure pass through an occluding reception interface, and fitna discriminates orientations at that interface.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a multi-layer reception barrier around Qur'anic recitation; I infer that the same interface governs the focus's vision and tree, while the live alternative is that the barrier describes only the earlier recitation scene.
structural_cues: The sequence runs recitation to hidden barrier in 17:45, then covered hearts and weighted ears to turned backs in 17:46.

activation_trace.role: Auditory perception establishes that material reaches the recipients before being reframed.
Secret counsel supplies the social chamber in which an alternative frame is produced.
Diversion and deception supplies the audience's counter-description of the messenger.
Directed sight or insight makes the competing representations an explicit object of inspection.
Forming and displaying a similitude supplies the production act of the counter-image.
A pictured likeness supplies the representational product imposed on the messenger.
Departure from the intended way supplies the directional effect of that substitution.
Showing anchors the competition in the focus's presented visual material.
Representation in tree form lets the recited tree function as a shaped image within the competition.

changed_reading.after: People actively metabolize the presented signs into rival representations, and that reframing is one mechanism by which warning becomes greater transgression.
changed_reading.before: People remain unmoved by the vision and tree.

context_deltas.mechanism: The audience listens, converts hearing into secret counsel, labels the messenger bewitched, and strikes its own similitudes. The focus's shown vision and tree-image are thus met by an active counter-image factory: recipients do not merely fail to see but substitute frames that redirect the sign.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies reception followed by hostile representation; I infer that the focus's images activate counter-images, while the live alternative is that the labels answer the messenger generally rather than the vision or tree.
structural_cues: Verse 17:47 moves from listening to private counsel and a label; 17:48 immediately identifies their act as striking similitudes and losing the way.

activation_trace.role: Pulverization and debris supplies the audience's material objection at its most disintegrated pole.
Rousing what is still supplies the opposed reactivation claimed to be impossible.
Hard stone supplies one imagined form of maximal resistance.
Iron and resistant hardness supplies the material specifically suited to an assay image.
The chest as the source of action locates imagined magnitude inside the resistant subject.
Opening and splitting supplies the creator's capacity to breach the hardened conception.
A verbal call supplies the eventual activation signal.
Answering speech supplies the response that penetrates the claimed resistance.
Testing metal transfers the preceding iron image into the focus's diagnostic mechanism.

changed_reading.after: Fitna becomes a material assay of recipients who imagine resistance as dust, stone, iron, or something still greater within themselves.
changed_reading.before: Fitna is a generic trial imposed on an abstract audience.

context_deltas.mechanism: The preceding challenge moves from pulverized remains to resurrection, stone, iron, and whatever seems greatest in the chest, before an originating fissure and an unavoidable call-response. Against that sequence, fitna as a metal assay answers an imagined hardened identity: the focus signs test what presents itself as unyielding material.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a material-hardness sequence immediately before fitna's assay branch; I infer that the signs assay a self-hardened reception posture, while the live alternative is that the material list serves only the resurrection argument.
structural_cues: Verses 17:49-52 progress from dust to stone and iron, to what is greater in the chest, to originating and answering a call.

activation_trace.role: Voiced speech supplies the medium in which the social mechanism operates.
Goodness opposed to ugliness marks the instructed alternative to conflict-producing speech.
Distance and severance supplies the adversarial tendency that breaks human relation.
Corrupting relations through incitement supplies the causal agitation between speakers.
The interval between parties supplies the relational space in which incitement branches.
The human collective supplies the same social field twice named in the focus.
Active enmity gives the branching speech network its hostile orientation.
Interlaced dispute and speech turns the focus tree into a model of ramifying social conflict.
Expulsion under displeasure marks that branching network as severed from good relation.
Growth supplies the propagation of conflict after warning enters the network.

changed_reading.after: The tree can also model a socially branching conflict structure through which warning is reprocessed and multiplied among people.
changed_reading.before: The cursed tree is an isolated object shown to individuals.

context_deltas.mechanism: The command to use better speech is motivated by an adversarial incitement that works between humans. This activates the focus tree's interlaced speech-conflict branch: a warning entering social exchange can ramify through hostile prompting until the cursed branching pattern and increasing transgression mirror one another.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies speech, interhuman incitement, and the tree branch of interlaced dispute; I infer propagation from warning through a hostile social network, while the live alternative keeps the tree wholly botanical and the speech warning merely adjacent.
structural_cues: Verse 17:53 repeats saying, locates incitement between humans, and immediately precedes the focus's repeated people, tree, warning, and increase.

activation_trace.role: Disclosure of the known to the knower assigns complete recipient knowledge to the Lord.
Messenger and message defines the addressee's delegated communicative role.
One who manages an affair by sufficiency and preservation names the role explicitly denied to the messenger.
Knowledge extending across heavens and earth expands the divine scope beyond the immediate audience.
Differentiated rank supplies a non-uniform distribution of prophetic roles within that scope.
One who reports from God supplies the prophetic transmission function.
Writing and book supplies another differentiated medium of transmission.
Lordship and sovereignty locates ownership of the encompassing field.
Complete enclosure in knowledge and possession anchors the divine side of the role distinction.

changed_reading.after: The counter-response does not negate the messenger's assigned act: enclosure governs outcomes, while showing and warning transmit without custodial control.
changed_reading.before: If the warning increases transgression, the communicative act appears to fail.

context_deltas.mechanism: Two statements of the Lord's knowledge surround the denial that the messenger was sent as custodian, followed by differentiated prophets and a written revelation. The focus's enclosure belongs to divine knowledge and governance; showing and warning belong to messenger transmission, not coercive control over the response.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies divine knowledge, messenger sending, and an explicit non-custodian clause; I infer a division between encompassing governance and non-coercive transmission, while the live alternative reads وكيل as denying only liability rather than control.
structural_cues: In 17:54-55, ربكم أعلم and وربك أعلم bracket the statement that the messenger was not sent as وكيل.

activation_trace.role: Removing a covering from harm supplies the relief falsely sought from subordinate objects.
Transformation from one state to another names the power those objects lack.
Seeking supplies an active orientation toward the Lord rather than away from warning.
Nearness opposed to distance gives that seeking a directional endpoint.
The heart's expectation of what is hoped for balances fear with attraction.
Fear as expectation of harm here contributes to approach and restraint rather than overflow.
Alert guarding against danger supplies fear's cautious output.
Inducing fear anchors the contrasting stimulus in the focus.
Sweeping overflow supplies the opposite output produced by resistant orientation.

changed_reading.after: Warning exposes direction: fear can orient a recipient toward proximity and caution or, under resistant reception, be converted into greater overflow.
changed_reading.before: Warning itself drives people into transgression.

context_deltas.mechanism: Those invoked besides God cannot uncover harm or transform it, while the invoked beings themselves seek proximity, hope for mercy, fear punishment, and remain cautious. Fear therefore is not a deterministic stimulus; its output depends on relational direction, producing approach and caution here but swelling transgression in the focus.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the same fear root in opposed response sequences; I infer that relational orientation mediates the effect, while the live alternative is that one fear belongs to worship and the other to warning without a designed contrast.
structural_cues: Verse 17:57 balances يَرْجُونَ with يَخَافُونَ and proximity-seeking; 17:60 repeats fear but follows it with increase into transgression.

activation_trace.role: Written fixation that entails judgment supplies the settled horizon behind the warning.
An ordered written line makes that horizon textually laid out before the sign discussion.
A barrier between an agent and an intended act supplies the restriction on spectacular sign sending.
Sending and dispatch supplies the governed movement of signs toward recipients.
A manifest mark identifies the dispatched material as publicly legible signs.
Assigning a sign to falsehood supplies the historical response that restricts further sending.
The she-camel and its concrete form supplies the exemplary material sign.
Direct visual perception marks that sign as conspicuous rather than evidentially obscure.
Putting a thing in the wrong place supplies the recipients' corrupt handling of the visible sign.
Inducing fear states the assigned function of dispatched signs immediately before the focus.
Showing anchors the focus vision as a mediated successor within the sign regime.
Recitation locates the tree sign in a textual medium rather than another demanded spectacle.
The repeated act of inducing fear directly continues the assigned function from 17:59.

changed_reading.after: They are contained, mediated signs deployed after spectacular signs have repeatedly been denied; their role is warning and diagnostic exposure, not escalation into an endless spectacle contest.
changed_reading.before: The vision and tree are two arbitrary tests whose warning happens to fail.

context_deltas.mechanism: A written horizon of communal destruction leads into an explicit restriction on sending signs because earlier peoples denied them. A conspicuously visible she-camel is then wrongfully handled, and sent signs are assigned the role of warning. The focus's vision and Qur'anic tree become mediated signs inside this restrained sign regime, with their counter-effect continuing the historical pattern rather than demanding ever more spectacle.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies direct adjacency, repeated warning morphology, sign restriction, and historical denial; I infer that the vision and tree are mediated signs selected within a restrained regime, while the live alternative treats 17:59 and 17:60 as separate examples without policy continuity.
structural_cues: Verse 17:59 ends وَمَا نُرْسِلُ بِالْآيَاتِ إِلَّا تَخْوِيفًا and 17:60 immediately continues وَنُخَوِّفُهُمْ فَمَا يَزِيدُهُمْ إِلَّا, while both verses pair visual signs with adverse reception.

remaining_uncertainties: The packet keeps dream vision, ocular or inward seeing, causative showing, and split-root narration or watering live; the exact medium of الرؤيا should remain unresolved.
The tree may remain a concrete botanical sign, a represented image, an interlaced social-conflict model, or an ecological analogy; the latter readings require explicit containment.
The syntax states that warning is followed by increase, but whether warning causes, occasions, exposes, or accelerates the recipients' own increase remains inferential.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Encompassed people turn disclosed images into assay material.** `ح و ط:B001/B004` surrounds and comprehends, `ر ء ي:B003/B012` dream-vision and making seen, `ف ت ن:B001` assays, `ش ج ر:B001/B009` tree and stock-origin, and `ط غ ي:B001/B002` rebels and overflows. Vision and tree are supplied inside comprehensive enclosure, but warning increases overflow. I infer the sign tests what orientation extracts from it. The ayah reads imagery as an assay whose reaction exposes the hearer.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 17:101–102 repeats seeing-sign, accusation, known insight, and ruin. The late Mosaic scene made the vision here part of a recurrent assay of whether disclosure becomes perception or overflow.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **The vision and tree as assay-media inside comprehensive enclosure.** Lexical evidence: `ح و ط B004` (complete grasp in knowledge or possession) in `أَحَاطَ`, `ف ت ن B001` (assaying by trial) in `فِتْنَةً`, `ش ج ر B002` (entangled dispute and speech) in `ٱلشَّجَرَةَ`, and `ط غ ي B002` (overflowing and overwhelming force) in `طُغْيَٰنًا`. Structural cue: 17:59 defines signs as warning and gives a visible sign that was wronged; here vision, tree, warning, increase, and overflow form a causal sequence, before 17:61–65 stages Iblis's challenge and bounded authority. Assigned role: enclosure secures the field, assay reveals what response contains, the tree becomes an entangled interpretive object, and repeated fear lets latent rebellion overflow visibly. Abductive move: warning-to-increase is explicit, but I infer that the increase reveals rather than escapes divine grasp. Reading change: the disputed images function diagnostically: they expose the tested population's disposition within an already comprehended field.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 17:61–65 completed the assay: Iblis's refusal, campaign, and sharply limited authority show what the trial reveals while correcting any deterministic reading of divine enclosure.

topics.reason: The unit noun and definite accusative form give the local tree a specified role.

topics.headline: earlier tree scenes echoed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears this tree against earlier tree scenes (2:35; 7:19), with the local tree functioning as Quran-located trial rather than garden prohibition.
topics.reason: The inter rows cite concrete earlier tree scenes at 2:35 and 7:19.

topics.headline: vision and tree as paired media
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees fitna operating through both a shown vision and a Quranic tree mention.
topics.reason: The row captures the syntactic pairing of semantically unlike objects.

words.gloss_range: definite passive participle describing the tree as curse-borne or mercy-excluded, not as an independent actor
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْمَلْعُونَةَ}} ({{tr:al-mal'ūnata}}) agrees with the tree as its identifying adjective and marks the tree as bearing curse-status. The passive participle makes the tree a recipient of exclusion from mercy; the following Quran-location can also be read as locating that curse-description in discourse. The same root can be applied to cursed people elsewhere (33:61).
words.root_gloss_range: curse, exclusion, and driving away from mercy or good; here expressed as a passive attribute borne by the tree

topics.headline: cursed adjective attached to tree
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees cursed as an identifying attribute of the tree, reinforced by agreement and paired feminine cadence.
topics.reason: The adjective matches the tree in definiteness, gender, and accusative case.

topics.headline: tree bears curse-status
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the tree bears exclusion-from-mercy status; it does not perform the curse.
topics.reason: The passive participle and l-ʿ-n semantics support received curse or exclusion from favor.

topics.headline: curse-status may be Quran-located
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can see the curse-description as potentially located in Quranic discourse, while the adjective still modifies the tree.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence allows the following fī phrase to modify the participle without detaching it from the tree.

topics.headline: curse lexeme transferred to a tree
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a moral-exclusion term normally applied to people also attached to a tree, with a human parallel at 33:61.
topics.reason: The inter row compares this tree adjective with cursed people at 33:61.

words.gloss_range: locative preposition placing the tree or curse inside Quranic discourse, with live attachment ambiguity
words.prose: {{ar:فِى}} ({{tr:fī}}) governs the Quran phrase and leaves a useful attachment ambiguity: the tree may be in the Quran, or its curse-status may be Quran-located. Either way, the trial arises from Quranic discourse, within Surah 17’s response chain of aversion, transgression, and loss (17:41; 17:82).

topics.headline: Quran-location attachment ambiguity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Quran-location may attach to the tree or to the cursed descriptor, giving two local reading routes without forcing one.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the Quran phrase, and attachment evidence allows both modification paths.

topics.headline: tree encountered in Quranic discourse
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the trial arising from a Quran-located object, not from a visible tree before the audience.
topics.reason: The prepositional phrase locates the relevant tree or curse in the Quranic text.

topics.headline: Quran-location inside increase-response chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader places this Quran-located trial inside Surah 17’s response chain of aversion, transgression, and loss (17:41; 17:82).
topics.reason: The supplied row links 17:41, 17:60, and 17:82 as a threefold increase-response pattern.

words.gloss_range: the recognized Quranic recitation/corpus as the textual location where the cursed tree is encountered
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْقُرْءَانِ}} ({{tr:al-Qur'āni}}) is the definite textual locus where the tree is encountered. Its root pressure of reciting and gathering makes the phrase a gathered recitation environment, and its hamza can be smoothed in variant recitation without changing that locus. Surah 17’s Quran references show revelation producing divergent responses (17:41; 17:45; 17:46; 17:82).
words.root_gloss_range: reciting, reading, and gathering; here the recognized gathered recitation or Quranic discourse as textual locus

topics.headline: Quran as textual location
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the recognized Quranic corpus as the place where the tree is encountered before the warning clause resumes.
topics.reason: The noun is definite and genitive under fī, closing the middle fitna beat.

topics.headline: gathered and recited discourse
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the tree inside a gathered recitation, not merely in abstract religious speech.
topics.reason: The q-r-ʾ evidence supports gathering and reciting as compatible pressures for the Quranic locus.

topics.headline: hamza smoothing in recitation noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a recitational pressure point in the name of the recitation itself, while the meaning remains the Quranic locus.
topics.reason: The variant drops the hamza phonetically without changing the local referent.

topics.headline: Surah 17 Quran-response pattern
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees this Quran reference among Surah 17 scenes where revelation exposes aversion, barriers, coverings, transgression, and loss (17:41; 17:45; 17:46; 17:82).
topics.reason: The inter rows give concrete Surah 17 Quran-response references.

words.gloss_range: resumptive connector shifting from completed trial-design to ongoing warning and its paradoxical outcome
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) resumes after the completed trial-design and shifts into ongoing warning. The hinge leads directly into the ayah’s paradox: warning is given, yet the response increases in transgression.

topics.headline: shift from design to warning
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the turn from completed trial-design into ongoing present warning and its paradoxical result.
topics.reason: The connector resumes or coordinates a new clause at the tense shift into nukhawwifuhum.

words.gloss_range: ongoing intensive divine warning or frightening directed at them, carrying both affective threat and protective warning force
words.prose: {{ar:نُخَوِّفُهُمْ}} ({{tr:nukhawwifuhum}}) is present, intensive warning directed at them. It enacts the warning purpose named in 17:59, keeps the divine We in the standard reading, contrasts with satanic fear-generation elsewhere (3:175), and sets up the same -hum group to become recipients of increase.
words.root_gloss_range: fear, fearing, warning, threatening, and causing fear; here Form II intensive warning/frightening directed at them

topics.headline: ongoing warning of the same recipients
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees present divine warning acting on the same people before they become recipients of increase.
topics.reason: The imperfect verb with attached -hum object opens the final warning-response beat.

topics.headline: intensive fear-causing as warning
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels warning as repeated affective pressure meant to alter response, not as neutral notification.
topics.reason: The Form II verb and kh-w-f semantics support intensive frightening, threat, and warning.

topics.headline: variant shifts divine agent expression
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a variant can express the agent as He, while the standard reading keeps the divine We directly present.
topics.reason: The variant changes person but does not replace the canonical first-person plural surface.

topics.headline: divine warning versus satanic intimidation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the same fear-generation form contrasted by agent: Satan frightens in one setting (3:175), while here God warns.
topics.reason: The inter row cites the Form II contrast at 3:175.

topics.headline: 17:59 warning purpose enacted
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the prior purpose of warning in 17:59 become a present act in 17:60, exposing failed reception.
topics.reason: The root echo carries takhwīf from 17:59 into the active verb here.

topics.headline: warned become increased recipients
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the same -hum group from being warned to being increased in transgression.
topics.reason: The same object suffix appears in nukhawwifuhum and yazīduhum.

words.gloss_range: consecutive fa that makes the following increase clause the paradoxical result of warning
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) makes the next clause the consequence slot of the warning. The particle carries causal sequence, but the content is adversative: warning leads, in this described case, only to greater transgression.

topics.headline: consequence marker as paradox pivot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the final clause as the immediate consequence slot of warning, made paradoxical by its content.
topics.reason: The particle links warning to outcome while the outcome reverses expected restraint.

words.gloss_range: negative particle opening the final restriction, clearing every outcome except increased transgression
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) opens the final restriction by negating every possible increase, including repentance, restraint, or benefit, before the exception. Together with the earlier restriction, it makes the ayah’s middle and end answer each other: only trial, then only transgression.

topics.headline: final negation-exception opening
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees every possible beneficial increase excluded before transgression is isolated.
topics.reason: The negative mā opens the second restriction before yazīduhum.

topics.headline: two restrictions close trial and outcome
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the middle and ending answer each other: only trial, then only transgression.
topics.reason: The repeated mā...illā frames create the ayah’s trial-outcome loop.

words.gloss_range: transitive increase applied to the same warned recipients, with transgression specifying what grows
words.prose: {{ar:يَزِيدُهُمْ}} ({{tr:yazīduhum}}) makes the warned group the recipients of increase, with {{ar:طُغْيَٰنًۭا}} ({{tr:ṭughyānan}}) naming what grows. The root is neutral amplification, capable of other outcomes such as humility (17:109), but here the object and specification make the increase negative and place it within Surah 17’s response scale (17:41; 17:82).
words.root_gloss_range: increase, addition, growth, and amplification without fixed moral direction; here the object and specification make the increase negative

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: transgression as the specified content of the increase

topics.headline: same recipients receive increase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the warned group as the same group grammatically receiving increased transgression.
topics.reason: The imperfect transitive verb carries the -hum object, and ṭughyānan specifies the increase.

topics.headline: neutral increase shaped by transgression
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that increase is morally neutral until the clause specifies transgression as what grows.
topics.reason: The root can amplify different states, including humility (17:109), but local object and specification make it negative here.

topics.headline: external subject increases them
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees increase happening to them through an external subject, not merely self-increase.
topics.reason: The chosen Form I transitive surface differs from derived self-increase patterns.

topics.headline: Surah 17 increase scale
topics.reader_payoff: The reader places this increase among Surah 17’s negative response scale: aversion, transgression, and loss (17:41; 17:82).
topics.reason: The rows connect z-y-d with the Quran-response and transgression fields in Surah 17.

words.gloss_range: exception particle that isolates transgression as the sole remainder after final negation
words.prose: {{ar:إِلَّا}} ({{tr:illā}}) closes the second restriction and leaves transgression as the sole semantic remainder. It mirrors the first exception so that only trial is paired with only transgression.

topics.headline: final exception isolates transgression
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees transgression left as the only positive remainder after negation.
topics.reason: The exception particle closes the second restriction and isolates ṭughyānan.

topics.headline: second exception mirrors the first
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees syntax pair only trial with only transgression.
topics.reason: The second illā mirrors the earlier exception before fitnatan.

words.gloss_range: indefinite verbal noun specifying the increase as boundary-overflowing transgression
words.prose: {{ar:طُغْيَٰنًۭا}} ({{tr:ṭughyānan}}) specifies the increase as boundary-overflowing transgression. Its root image of flood beyond limits, its pressure toward overreaching authority, and the revelation-response parallels (5:64; 5:68) make the final result a reversal of warning’s expected restraint from 17:59. Its -an cadence ties the close back to trial and greatness as the scene expands from private address to the resistant people.
words.root_gloss_range: overflowing, exceeding bounds, rebellion, and tyrannical overreach; here the increase is specified as moral boundary-overflow

topics.headline: transgression as measurable increase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees transgression not as a side label but as the named measurable content of the increase.
topics.reason: The indefinite verbal noun functions as the specification or object domain after yazīduhum.

topics.headline: boundary-overflow and overreach
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels transgression as overflow past limits, with pressure toward tyrannical overreach.
topics.reason: The t-gh-y evidence supports overflow and false-authority pressure compatible with local moral transgression.

topics.headline: increase-in-transgression formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees this clause inside a wider formula where revelation exposes and amplifies rebellion in deniers (5:64; 5:68).
topics.reason: The supplied inter rows name the same increase-in-transgression construction at 5:64 and 5:68.

topics.headline: warning answered by overflow
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees warning meant to restrain answered by boundary-overflow instead, linking back to the warning purpose in 17:59.
topics.reason: The rows explicitly contrast takhwīf in 17:59 with ṭughyān in 17:60.

topics.headline: cadence and boundary zoom
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears trial, overflow, and magnitude tied by cadence while the scene expands back from private address to the resistant people.
topics.reason: The sound and boundary rows add distinct closure and zoom payoffs.

words.gloss_range: indefinite accusative adjective scaling the transgression as great, with moral magnitude supplied by what it modifies
words.prose: {{ar:كَبِيرًۭا}} ({{tr:kabīran}}) closes by scaling the transgression. The adjective is morally directed by the noun it modifies, can carry arrogance-pressure, echoes a severe-noun construction at 33:68, and reverses the opening containment image by ending with great overflow under divine encompassing. Its long ī plus tanwīn-alif gives the final moral verdict a lingering cadence.
words.root_gloss_range: greatness, largeness, magnitude, significance, pride, and arrogance; here it scales transgression as a severe moral magnitude

topics.headline: great as dependent scale modifier
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the ayah end not just with transgression but with transgression scaled by its final dependent adjective.
topics.reason: The adjective agrees with ṭughyānan in accusative indefiniteness and closes the ayah.

topics.headline: magnitude with arrogance pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the scale word takes its moral direction from transgression and can carry pride-swollen force here.
topics.reason: The k-b-r range is morally ambivalent, but local attachment to transgression fixes negative scale.

topics.headline: great severe-noun construction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can compare this great transgression to a great curse construction (33:68), while the local noun remains transgression.
topics.reason: The row cites the same adjective scaling a severe moral noun at 33:68.

topics.headline: Surah scale and containment reversal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the close reverse the opening image: people under divine encompassing still overflow into a scaled moral extreme, one of Surah 17’s large consequence terms (17:4; 17:9; 17:31).
topics.reason: The rows connect the ending scale to the opening encompassing and to Surah 17 scale markers.

topics.headline: heavy final cadence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the final long cadence linger on the enlarged moral verdict.
topics.reason: The prosody row gives a distinct final-sound payoff.
